tasks.short: Analyse failures and document corrective recommendations.

steps.what: Inspect actual failed equipment and gather failure observations and test evidence
outputs: actual mechanical failure observations and readings

steps.what: Transfer and check actual failure test data in the engineering analysis system {OTHER}
inputs: actual mechanical failure observations and readings

steps.what: Conduct failure analyses and choose justified corrective actions with engineering staff
outputs: actual failure interpretation and chosen corrective recommendations

steps.what: Document actual failure analysis results and corrective-action recommendations
inputs: actual failure interpretation and chosen corrective recommendations

loop.purpose: Draft the failure report from actual technician findings
loop.input: Verified evidence, chosen failure interpretation and corrective recommendations
loop.check: Technician checks causal meaning, omitted alternative causes, unsupported corrective claims and actual test evidence
loop.stop: Missing actual finding or two failed revisions returns writing to manual work
loop.why_not_simpler: Native result fields and report headings come first; failure explanations vary

steps.what: Check the final failure report, evidence and actual engineering recipients
Save the checked final mechanical failure report
Send the checked failure report and recommendations to actual internal engineering recipients

tasks.design: Configure native test-data import in the engineering analysis system {OTHER}, then use fixed report fields before a bounded draft in {DOCS}. The technician inspects, analyses and chooses recommendations with actual engineering staff, checks the exact final report and separately saves and sends it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Failure work can repeat test-data entry and explanatory report writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native input mappings and bounded source-linked prose can reduce transcription and first-draft writing.
tasks.still_hard: Failure causes, alternative explanations and safe corrective actions require engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician connects physical evidence to the actual equipment history and avoids a plausible but unsupported cause.
tasks.altitude: Less evidence transfer and report drafting; engineering decision rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: engineering test imports and bounded report drafting can support failure records; they do not determine root cause or authorise a corrective change.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual failure analysis, documentation and internal recommendation delivery. Corrective implementation remains an actual authorised owner action with no avoided labour claimed.

Technician creates actual observations and sample/equipment identifiers in s1; instruments provide actual timestamp, reading and unit. Technician verifies mapping and missing history in s2 and manually captures unsupported evidence. Actual cause and recommendation are chosen in s3 before report drafting.
Test native imports and fixed report fields before code. Existing imports earn no saving. Meaning correction remains in s4; inspection, cause assessment and the complete final check remain retained.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Routine save and send each retain one percent and use the existing report check without added approval time.
unknowns: What test data is still typed twice?
research_questions: Does bounded drafting save time after checking alternative causes and corrective-action meaning?

incremental.description: Maintain test mappings and failure-report drafting checks.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final mechanical failure report and exact document destination; edits require recheck
s5 checked final mechanical failure report and exact internal recipients; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15*0.50 data entry + 14*0.30 report prose = 11.7; minus 1.5 upkeep = 10.2. With half of entry and prose eligible, 5.85 minus 1.5 = 4.35. Actual failure judgement and save/send time remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist engineers with machinery or product development and testing.

steps.what: Review actual engineer instructions and equipment or product requirements
Assist engineers in choosing actual development, test or manufacture work
Prepare actual development drawings or test fixtures in the engineering drawing system {OTHER}
outputs: actual development drawing or fixture draft

steps.what: Perform actual authorised machinery or product development, testing or manufacturing assistance
inputs: actual development drawing or fixture draft
outputs: actual mechanical development observations and results

steps.what: Write and check actual development or test findings and drawing references
inputs: actual mechanical development observations and results
actual development drawing or fixture draft

steps.what: Save the checked actual mechanical development record

tasks.design: Reuse actual component geometry and drawing references in the engineering drawing system {OTHER}. The technician works with engineers and performs actual development or testing personally; only repeated drawing and fixture-layout entry changes, and actual findings remain manually captured and checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Development assistance can redraw unchanged components in fixture or test drawings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native component references can reduce repeated geometry entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical setup, manufacture, test behaviour and following actual engineering direction require hands-on skill.
tasks.human_edge: The technician sees when a drawing or fixture is not workable with the actual equipment.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated drawing entry; engineer-directed work and responsibility stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: engineering drawing tools can reuse approved component geometry in development fixtures and layouts; actual development, testing and manufacture remain physical work.

assumptions: Design, development, testing and manufacture assistance are alternative branches. This provisional mix includes actual drawing work where used; reweight physical-only work rather than adding a drawing requirement.

Engineer supplies actual brief, approved component revision and authorised work instructions; technician verifies context in s1-s2 and manually completes unsupported geometry in s3. Actual observations and results arise in s4 and are captured in s5. No free test findings are assumed.

Native drawing reference configuration comes before code. Existing reused geometry earns no saving. Engineer approval of any actual executable test or manufacturing setup remains a real source dependency, not avoided other-role work.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. The final save retains one percent and uses the existing development-record check without extra approval time.
unknowns: How much component geometry is redrawn?
What actual assistance branches involve drawings?
research_questions: Does native geometry reuse reduce actual fixture/layout entry after current component-library reuse is counted?

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final actual mechanical development record and exact document destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.40 repeated geometry = 8; minus 1 upkeep = 7. If half the geometry is reusable, 4 minus 1 = 3. Engineer discussion, physical work and findings writing remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare machinery, tool, plant or equipment layouts.

steps.what: Verify actual machinery dimensions, services, clearances and plant constraints
Choose workable machinery, tool, plant or equipment arrangement with engineering staff
Prepare layouts of machinery, tools, plants or equipment in the drawing system {OTHER}
Check the final layout dimensions, clearances, services and revision
Save the checked final mechanical layout drawing

tasks.design: Configure actual equipment blocks and facility references in the engineering drawing system {OTHER}. The technician verifies dimensions, chooses the arrangement with engineering staff and checks the final layout before saving; native reuse changes repeated drawing entry only.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layout revisions can redraw unchanged machines, tools and facility geometry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native component blocks and referenced facility geometry can reduce repeated drawing work.
tasks.still_hard: Maintenance access, services and practical plant flow require layout judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician notices a physically impractical arrangement despite a neat drawing.
tasks.altitude: Less layout redrawing; arrangement and engineering authority stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: drawing tools support reusable equipment blocks and facility references; actual layout suitability remains engineering judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is actual layout preparation through its checked saved revision. Installation and actual engineering release remain owner actions with no saved labour claimed.

Equipment owner supplies actual identifier, envelope, service connections and drawing revision; facility owner supplies actual reference geometry. Technician checks in s1 and manually enters missing or incompatible geometry in s3. No free field survey is assumed.

Test native blocks and references before code. Existing component reuse earns no saving. Only repeated geometry changes; constraint reading, arrangement choice and complete final layout checking remain human.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Same-system save retains one percent and uses the existing layout check without extra approval time.
unknowns: How much equipment geometry is already reused?
Are source dimensions and revisions reliable?
research_questions: Can actual layout revisions reuse components without masking changed clearances or source revisions?

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final mechanical layout, exact drawing revision and document destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 40*0.40 repeated drawing entry = 16; minus 1 upkeep = 15. With half the geometry reusable, 8 minus 1 = 7. Arrangement choices, final checks and save time remain unchanged.

tasks.short: Prepare equipment inspection and reliability schedules or work records.

steps.what: Collect and verify actual equipment, inspection and reliability history
Select applicable inspection intervals, reliability criteria and work-planning constraints
outputs: chosen equipment scheduling rules and exceptions

steps.what: Calculate inspection due dates and reliability schedule entries from the actual selected rules
inputs: chosen equipment scheduling rules and exceptions

steps.what: Prepare equipment inspection schedules, reliability schedules, work plans or other records
inputs: chosen equipment scheduling rules and exceptions
outputs: draft equipment schedule or work-plan record

steps.what: Check the final equipment schedule, work plan, exceptions and asset destinations
inputs: draft equipment schedule or work-plan record
chosen equipment scheduling rules and exceptions
outputs: checked final equipment schedule or work plan

steps.what: Commit the checked equipment schedule or work plan to its actual asset records
inputs: checked final equipment schedule or work plan
outputs: saved checked equipment schedule or work plan

tasks.design: Configure existing asset-history links, due-date formulas and schedule fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The technician verifies source history, selects applicable approved intervals and exceptions, checks the complete final schedule and separately commits it; the configuration does not create maintenance policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedules can repeat asset/history entry, due-date arithmetic and copying calculated fields into work plans.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling and asset-linked records can reduce these repeated calculations and entries.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability of intervals, unreliable history and exceptional equipment risks require engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician spots a schedule that is arithmetically valid but unsuitable for the actual equipment condition.
tasks.altitude: Less schedule entry and arithmetic; maintenance policy and exception authority stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: maintenance systems can reuse asset history, calculate dates from approved intervals and populate draft work-plan fields; policy and exception judgement remain human.

assumptions: Inspection schedules, reliability schedules, work plans and other records are alternative outputs. Reweight to actual work; boundary is preparing and saving them, not performing inspections or declaring equipment reliable.

Asset/history owners supply actual asset identifier, last completed inspection date, meter reading, source status and revision. Actual maintenance criteria owner supplies approved interval and unit; technician verifies sources in s1 and selects applicable rules and exceptions in s2. Missing history, ambiguous units and unsupported exceptions stay manual before s3.

Test native scheduling and linked fields before code. Existing automatic due dates, existing populated work plans and background runtime earn no new labour saving. Only actual manual repeated transfer, arithmetic and field entry qualify; no notification or work dispatch is added.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Final commit retains one percent and uses the existing schedule check without added approval time.
unknowns: Which schedules are already generated natively?
Are last-completed dates and meter units reliable?
research_questions: Can configured dates and work-plan fields reproduce actual schedules including exceptions without hiding stale source history?

incremental.description: Maintain asset-history mappings and checked interval/work-plan configuration.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final equipment schedule or work plan, exact asset records and schedule version; edits void approval
